page: Amazon Web Services m7i.48xlarge is a heavy-footprint general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. Computational capacity is driven by Intel Xeon 8488C processors, supplying 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated virtual CPUs clocked at 3.2 GHz. The processor architecture includes 105 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 instruction sets. Memory provisioning consists of 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 4 GB per vCPU general-purpose ratio.

Network communication is rated at a 50 Gbps baseline, providing sustained throughput for distributed services and storage communication. The instance does not include local bundled NVMe or SSD storage, requiring external network-attached block storage for operating system installations and persistent application state. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addressing is omitted.

Benchmark results confirm exceptional aggregate throughput across parallelized workloads. The instance registers top-tier scores in multi-core CPU testing, uncached memory read bandwidth of 455.06 GB/sec, and 182.23 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. In static web serving benchmarks, throughput reaches 128.6 GB/sec, complemented by strong CPU inference performance across varying LLM parameter sizes. The architectural tradeoff is average single-thread performance compared to specialized high-frequency instances. The massive core density and rapid DDR5 memory make it technically suited for scale-up relational databases, in-memory caching layers, backend API fleets, and continuous data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.48xlarge is a high-capacity general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from 96 physical Intel Xeon 8488C cores running at 3.2 GHz, paired with 768 GB of DDR5 system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AMX and AVX-512 vector acceleration, which benefits matrix calculations and cryptographic operations. The instance delivers a baseline networking throughput of 50 Gbps and includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the m7i.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution and high memory bandwidth, achieving 182.23 million Redis SET operations per second and 128.6 GB/sec in static web serving. While single-threaded performance remains moderate, the massive core density and fast DDR5 subsystem make it well matched for distributed databases, high-concurrency microservices, caching clusters, and large CPU-based data processing pipelines.
